name: Weathered Wayfarer
oracle_text: {W}, {T}: Search your library for a land card, reveal it, put it into your hand, then shuffle. Activate only if an opponent controls more lands than you.
blocked_sentences: {W}, {T}: Search your library for a land card, reveal it, put it into your hand, then shuffle. Activate only if an opponent controls more lands than you.

needs.what: A value leaf that counts matching objects **one player at a time** and aggregates existentially or universally, so a condition can ask "does any single opponent control more lands than I do". Concretely the pair `{"max_count_of": {"player": "each_opponent", "objects": {"zone": "battlefield", "types": ["Land"]}}}` (the existential -- "an opponent controls more X than you") and `{"min_count_of": ...}` (the universal -- "each opponent controls more X than you"), mirroring the existing `min_life_of` / `max_life_of` split and for exactly the reason recorded in the comment above them in `engine/effects/values.py`. Implementation: add both names to `VALUE_KEYS`, evaluate by running `resolve_pool` once per player returned by `select_players(ctx, spec["player"])` with the pool scoped to that single player (the evaluator injects the scope itself, the way `for_each_player` injects `each_player`, since a card written outside a loop has no binding to name), and give `validate_value` the matching branch so a misspelling is a load error rather than a silent 0. For this card it must be reachable from an **activated ability's** `condition` -- the field that already carries "Activate only if you control five or more Vampires" on bloodline_keeper -- so no new plumbing is needed beyond the leaf itself, and the activation gate must be re-checked at activation time (it is an activation restriction, not an intervening-if: unlike a trigger's condition it is never rechecked on resolution).
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `count` is the only object-counting leaf and it resolves a single merged pool: `{"count": {"zone": "battlefield", "controller": "opponent", "types": ["Land"]}}` **sums across the whole table**, because `matches` and `_zone_players` in `engine/effects/selectors.py` treat `controller: "opponent"` as "every opponent at once" -- the code says so in a comment there. `lands_you_control` reads only your own side, so it can supply the right-hand side of the comparison and nothing else. `min_life_of`/`max_life_of` are exactly the right shape but are hard-wired to life totals. `exists` filters objects and cannot relate a land's controller's land count back to yours; `distinct` counts distinct values over one pool; `extreme` ranks only on power/toughness/mana_value. The one per-player mechanism that does exist -- `for_each_player` with `controller: {"binding": "each_player"}` -- is an **op**, so it cannot appear in an activated ability's `condition` at all, and moving the test into `effects` would be a different card: it would make the ability legal to activate whenever any board state existed, paying {W} and the tap for nothing when you are ahead on lands, and would run the tutor once per qualifying opponent.
needs.why_it_cannot_be_approximated: Summing opponents' lands unlocks the ability in games where the printed card is dead: at a four-player pod three opponents holding two lands each total 6 and beat your 5, so a Wayfarer built on `count` + `controller: "opponent"` is a repeatable one-mana unconditional land tutor -- one of the strongest cards in the format -- while the real card is switched off whenever you are not behind. Dropping the restriction is the same card with the gate always open. Dropping the whole ability leaves a vanilla {W} 1/1 whose only printed line does nothing.

notes:
Only the activation restriction blocks this card; the rest of the line is expressible today. Once the leaf exists the whole card is one activated ability: `cost: {"mana": "{W}", "tap": true}` (both in cost_keys), `condition: {"cmp": ">", "left": {"max_count_of": {"player": "each_opponent", "objects": {"zone": "battlefield", "types": ["Land"]}}}, "right": {"lands_you_control": true}}`, and effects of a single `search_library` with `count: 1`, `selector: {"types": ["Land"]}` -- no `supertypes: ["Basic"]`, the card says "a land card" -- and no explicit `destination` or `shuffle` op, since `_search` in engine/effects/ops_cards.py already defaults `destination` to "hand" and computes `shuffles = "library" in zones and spec.get("shuffle", True)`, which is the printed "then shuffle". The printed "reveal it" is a public-information step of the search itself, not a separate `reveal` op. The `text` on that one ability is the whole printed line including the restriction sentence, so the residual gate is satisfied. The starting_point (1/1 Human Nomad Cleric, {W}, mono-white) needs no change.

Sandbox note for whoever closes this: the ability is activated, and the harness only casts the card and stops, so the eventual answer's expectation must be `{"zone": "battlefield", "battlefield_count": 33}` -- never a fetched land. It is doubly unobservable there, since in the fixed position you control 30 lands to the opponent's 2 and the restriction is false anyway. The condition and the tutor need an engine unit test on a board where one opponent is ahead on lands, plus a pod-shaped case where the opponents' lands only beat yours in aggregate and the ability must stay unactivatable.

Same capability and same leaf as the existing gap record for knight_of_the_white_orchid, which needs it in a trigger's intervening-if rather than an activation restriction -- closing one closes both. Other queued members of the family: Loyal Warhound, Claim Jumper, Scouting Hawk, Space Marine Scout, Beza the Bounding Spring, Aerial Surveyor, Boreas Charger, Cartographer's Hawk (all the "more lands than you" cards), plus Avatar of Might and Advice from the Fae for the creature-count and `min_count_of` variants.
